## R Tidyverse vs. Python Pandas vs. Python Polars

This reference table outlines the structural translation layer between traditional data manipulation frameworks and modern, high-performance query engines.

 > <sub>Note: Operations in <span style="color: #08519c;">blue</span> are global, console operations

| Operation | R (dplyr / tidyverse) | Pandas Method Chain | Polars Expression Chain |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Filter Rows** | `filter(col > 50)` | `.query("amount > 50")` | `.filter(pl.col("amount") > 50)` |
| **Filter Multiple (AND)** | `filter(A > 10, B == "X")` | `.query("A > 10 and B == 'X'")` | `.filter(pl.col("A") > 10, pl.col("B") == "X")` |
| **Mutate Columns** | `mutate(fee = amt * 0.02)` | `.assign(fee = lambda df: ...)` | `.with_columns(fee = pl.col("amt") * 0.02)` |
| **Select Columns** | `select(col1, col2)` | <code><span style="color: #d9534f; font-weight: bold;">[DATAFRAME_OBJECT]</span>[["col1","col2"]]</code> | `.select("col1", "col2")` |
| **Select "All BUT" Columns**| `select(!c(col2, col5))` | <code>.loc[:, ~<span style="color: #d9534f; font-weight: bold;">[DATAFRAME_OBJECT]</span>.columns<br>.isin(["col2","col5"])]</code> | `.select(pl.all().exclude(["col2", "col5"]))` |
| **Sort Rows** | `arrange(col1)` | `.sort_values(by="col1")` | `.sort("col1")` |
| **Optimize Top Rows** | `slice_max(amt, n=3)` | `.nlargest(3, "amt")` | `.top_k(3, by="amt")` |
| **Group Data** | `group_by(category)` | `.groupby("category")` | `.group_by("category")` |
| **Aggregate** | `summarise(rev = sum(amt))` | `.agg(rev=("amt", "sum"))` | `.agg(pl.col("amt").sum().alias("rev"))` |
| **Type Cast** | `as.numeric(col)` | <code>.assign(col3 = lambda df: pd.to_numeric(df["col3"], errors="coerce"))</code> | `.cast(pl.Float64, strict=False)` |
| **Clean Strings** | `str_to_lower(col)` | <code>.assign(col3 = lambda df: df["col3"].str.lower())</code> | `.with_columns(pl.col("col3").str.to_lowercase())` |
| **Rename** | `rename_with(~ str_to_lower(str_trim(.)))` | `.rename(columns=lambda c: c.strip().lower())` | <code>.rename({c: c.strip().lower() for c in<br> <span style="color: #d9534f; font-weight: bold;">[DATAFRAME_OBJECT]</span>.collect_schema().names()})</code> |
| <span style="color: #08519c; font-weight: bold;">Limit Col Length</span> | <code><span style="color: #08519c;">options(pillar.width=40)</span></code> | <code><span style="color: #08519c;">.set_option("display.max_colwidth",25)</span></code> | <code><span style="color: #08519c;">.Config.set_fmt_str_lengths(25)</span></code> |

---

### Object Dependency & Expressive Coupling

While most of the above syntax are object-agnostic, there are a few above that *do* require a direct reference to the parent object. Such exceptions are listed with the specific parent reference in <span style="color: #d9534f; font-weight: bold;">[red bold text]</span>. I will also list such exceptions below.

* <code><span style="color: #d9534f; font-weight: bold;">[DATAFRAME_OBJECT]</span>[["col1","col2"]]</code>
* <code>.loc[:, ~<span style="color: #d9534f; font-weight: bold;">[DATAFRAME_OBJECT]</span>.columns.isin(["col2","col5"])]</code>
* <code>.rename({c: c.strip().lower() for c in <span style="color: #d9534f; font-weight: bold;">[DATAFRAME_OBJECT]</span>.collect_schema().names()})</code>

### 🧠 Critical Structural Architecture Notes

#### 1. The Polars Multi-Argument Shortcut (Dropping `[...]`)
In both `.filter()` and `.agg()`, Polars allows you to completely drop Python list brackets `[...]` and pass expressions as simple comma-separated arguments. 

* **Filters:** Commas are automatically interpreted as a logical `AND`. This completely eliminates the nightmare of nesting matching parentheses like `((condition_a) & (condition_b))`.
* **Aggregations:** Dropping the list bracket allows you to cleanly list each metric on a brand-new vertical line, maximizing scannability.

#### 2. The `.top_k()` Heap-Select Shift
When your goal is finding the highest or lowest values in a pipeline, break the traditional habit of running `.sort().head()`. 

Using `.top_k()` triggers Polars' internal **Heap-Select algorithm**. Instead of using heavy computational overhead to sort millions of rows just to discard 99% of them, Polars dynamically tracks only the top records at the file-scan level, preserving memory and execution speed.

#### 3. The Polars Expression Console Context Rule
The internal engine differentiates strictly between mutating a whole dataframe and evaluating a column slice. 
* If the background parser knows you are modifying a DataFrame/LazyFrame object, your execution environment is safe.
* If you attempt to edit text downstream of an active, unclosed `pl.col()` expression without assigning it proper structural scope, the engine loses track of its columnar position and will throw an immediate error.
